transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-02-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Nora Patel (Redwood Product) -- Ethan Park (CTO, Peregrine), Sasha Li (Lead ML Eng), Priya Menon (Security), Mark Walker (PM)

Summary (auto): quick pilot proposal focused on schema-enforced tool calling (JSON mode), runtime guardrails, and KMS/VPC security requirements. Customer wants a short pilot to validate financial reconciliation workflows with strict typed outputs and controlled tool invocations.

00:00 Maya: alright everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time. we sent an agenda -- quick intros, demo of JSON-mode tooling + Console flow, then discuss pilot scope and security questions.
00:12 Ethan: thanks maya, quick note — time zones are fun, we're on a tight timeline, need pilot started by mid-march ideally.
:-- 00:20 Maya: got it, we'll push for that. diego, want to kick off the demo?
00:23 Diego: yeah i'll share my screen — one sec, uh screen's up? can you see the Console? (pause)
00:30 Speaker 1: yep seeing it.
00:35 Diego: great. first, JSON mode — the idea is enforceable response contracts. you define a schema for the action the model should return, we validate at runtime and optionally route to a tool if the schema indicates 'call_tool: true'. here's an example for Peregrine: a reconciliation action with fields {transaction_id, amount_delta, confidence, action} where action is enum ["auto-adjust","flag-for-review","create-incident"].
01:05 Sasha: wait, can the schema require nested arrays? our reconciliations sometimes return multiple candidate matches.
01:12 Diego: yep — arrays of candidates supported, and we also surface a per-token validation trace in the Console so you can see where the model deviated. sometimes the transcript shows token-level mismatches — we log it.
01:30 Mark: and if the model outputs something outside the enum, do you auto-fallback?
01:35 Diego: configurable. you can set policy to either deny-and-fail, coerce with a fallback path, or call a secondary model for correction. for Peregrine's use-case i'd suggest 'reject + call correction model' for auditability.
01:50 Priya: important — any time there's a tool call that touches internal accounting systems, we need strong auth, KMS-wrapped keys, and audit trails. how does that look?
02:02 Nora: good question. Redwood Private gives you a VPC option where control plane sits inside your network, and keys are managed via your KMS. for hosted pilots we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) and every tool call is logged with request ID, user, and the schema payload snapshot.
02:20 Priya: ok, can you show the audit log example?
02:25 Diego: sure loading. here's an audit entry sample, note there's a 'schema_version' and 'tool_signature' field. sometimes the transcription parser garbles names, you'll see 'kv cache' and 'k v cache' in older exports — just an FYI.
02:42 Ethan: performance — we need sub-200ms p50 for lookups in the recon flow, is that realistic?
02:49 Diego: depends on batching and sequence length. for single-turn recon (1k tokens) p50 of ~180-220ms on dedicated gpus is achievable; for longer 4k sequences we recommend continuous KV caching and a quantized runtime profile. we can run a bench against your real prompt set in the pilot.
03:10 Sasha: what's the plan for tool authentication? we can't expose DB creds to the model host.
03:15 Diego: we use short-lived signed tokens for tool invocation — Redwood calls an internal proxy that you host in the VPC; proxy uses your KMS to sign/verify, and the model host only sees an opaque token. this avoids direct credential sharing.
03:30 Priya: do you support HSM-backed keys?
03:35 Nora: yes, HSM via supported KMS vendors. we'll include the compatibility matrix in the security pack.
03:42 Mark: back to schema enforcement — can we add guardrails like 'max changes per call' and 'require human review if confidence < 0.85'?
03:50 Diego: absolutely. you can express policy at the route level in the Console: schema + policy rules. when confidence falls below threshold, the Route returns a 'review_required' action instead of calling tool. those policies are versioned and can be canaried.
04:10 Ethan: what about retries and dedup? financial systems hate duplicates.
04:16 Diego: we support idempotency keys on calls and automatic dedup logic in the tool adapter. we also surface a 'dedup-score' in logs so you can tune heuristics.
04:30 Maya: quick walkthrough of the pilot we propose: 6-week pilot, stage 1 (week 1-2) — schema design + sandbox mapping; stage 2 (week 3-4) — private pilot in your VPC or dedicated instance with KMS integration, run bench tests; stage 3 (week 5-6) — iterate, add fallback flows, and produce final runbook.
04:58 Ethan: cost — high-level numbers? we need to justify to finance.
05:05 Maya: for pilot we have a fixed pilot bundle: reserved instance time + 100k tokens of test traffic + 2x bench runs. we'll add detailed pricing in SOW. after pilot, you can move to Dedicated reserved capacity with predictable throughput pricing.
05:20 Sasha: any competitor gotchas? we evaluated openai and anthropic; they don't offer schema-enforced tool routing out-of-the-box, so we'd have to build orchestration ourselves.
05:32 Maya: exactly. Redwood's differentiator here is built-in typed responses and tool orchestration with observability — reduces engineering lift.
05:44 Mark: can we see a short end-to-end example: model returns JSON -> policy -> tool call -> audit?
05:50 Diego: sure, quick demo. (demo run) model returned a candidate with action 'auto-adjust', confidence 0.92, we matched transaction_id, and Console shows the call queued to ToolAdapter v2. ToolAdapter performs idempotency check, posts to your internal reconcile endpoint, returns 200, Redwood records event and emits webhook to your downstream systems.
06:30 Sasha: small nit — sometimes model hallucinations include extraneous fields, how strict is validation?
06:36 Diego: strict by default — we reject unknown fields unless you opt into 'allow_extra' mode. you can also use sanitizers that map alternate field names; we keep per-field provenance traces.
06:50 Priya: security quickfire: SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit retention — what are defaults and what can be extended?
06:58 Nora: SSO with SAML/SCIM supported, RBAC roles for reader/operator/admin, audit retention configurable (30/90/365 days) for pilot we recommend 90 days. for enterprise we can offer extended retention as an add-on.
07:20 Ethan: about privacy — can we ensure model logs don't persist raw PII?
07:26 Diego: yes — we support PII redaction rules at ingestion and store only token-level metrics by default. if you need full encryption at rest, that's via your KMS/HSM in the Private deployment.
07:46 Mark: what's the rollback story if a model starts misbehaving in production?
07:50 Diego: Console supports pinned model versions per-route, automatic fallback to a compatible model variant, and weighted canary rollouts. we also have an 'auto-disable-on-regression' option tied to eval runs.
08:06 Sasha: one operational question — do we need to change our DB schema to support tool responses?
08:12 Diego: minimal change: tool adapter returns a normalized payload, you can map fields via a small transform layer. we supply a transform template library for common ERP/Accounting systems.
08:30 Maya: we should talk about observability — token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency, and the schema mismatch dashboard.
08:36 Liam: jumping in — Console has a Schema Errors dashboard that groups failures by field and by prompt template; you can attach example prompts to each failure for triage. there's also a replay feature for failed calls.
08:58 Ethan: can we run a bench that reproduces our high-concurrency night batch? we do spikes up to 400QPS for end-of-day processing.
09:06 Diego: yes, bench harness can simulate spike patterns and show us where latency tails creep up. for that scale we'd recommend Dedicated with autoscale policies tuned to your peak window.
09:20 Priya: any legal procurement items we should expect? SOC2 reports, DPA, cross-border data?
09:28 Maya: yes we'll share SOC2, DPA, and proposed data residency options. for cross-border we have configuration for region pinning or Private on-prem if required.
09:42 Sasha: about schema evolution — how do we roll a change without breaking production?
09:48 Diego: schemas are versioned. Console supports a 'compatibility check' run where we run a sample prompt set against the new schema in a sandbox to surface incompatible changes before rollout.
10:05 Mark: ok sounds good. any showstoppers on your side?
10:10 Ethan: one — we need to ensure KMS and HSM compatibility with our vendor (Thales).
10:14 Nora: we'll check the compatibility matrix; if needed we can provision a dedicated gateway.
10:20 Maya: wrapping up — recap of agreed points and pilot outline. i'll send SOW and security pack. diego will run bench plan and liaise with sasha. we'll try to lock the tech run for 2027-02-18.
10:35 Ethan: thanks, one more quick question — do you have a sample schema for our reconciliation we can iterate on?
10:40 Diego: yes i'll drop an initial schema and a postman collection to the shared folder.
10:46 Mark: thanks all, excited to try this.
